question: What does population health nursing primarily focus on?

options.A: The financial balance sheet of a health clinic
options.B: The health outcomes of an entire group of people
options.C: The surgical procedures performed in a single hospital ward
options.D: The genetic profile of an individual patient

explanation: Population health looks beyond the individual patient to protect and promote the well-being of whole communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: How does incidence differ from prevalence in community health data?

options.A: Incidence counts deaths, while prevalence counts active infections
options.B: Incidence is calculated yearly, while prevalence is calculated daily
options.C: Incidence measures new cases over time, while prevalence measures total existing cases
options.D: Incidence only applies to children, while prevalence applies to adults

explanation: Incidence tracks how fast a disease is spreading by counting new cases, whereas prevalence shows how widespread a condition currently is within the population. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the main shift that occurs during an epidemiological transition?

options.A: A shift from infectious diseases to chronic non-communicable diseases
options.B: A shift from high birth rates to zero population growth
options.C: A shift from urban living to rural farming settlements
options.D: A shift from hospital care to traditional healing practices

explanation: As societies develop and life expectancy increases, the primary health burden moves away from acute infections toward chronic lifestyle and age-related illnesses. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why do developing communities often face a double burden of disease?

options.A: Every patient is diagnosed with at least two separate diseases at the same time
options.B: They deal with ongoing infectious illnesses while also seeing a rise in chronic lifestyle conditions
options.C: Healthcare workers must split their time equally between cities and villages
options.D: They have two different ministries of health competing for funding

explanation: The double burden means communities are still fighting poverty-related infections like malaria while simultaneously managing rising rates of hypertension and diabetes. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of a social determinant of health?

options.A: The personal willpower of an individual to avoid sickness
options.B: Access to safe drinking water and sanitation
options.C: The specific genetic blood type of a patient
options.D: The brand of medication prescribed by a doctor

explanation: Social determinants are external environmental, economic, and social conditions that powerfully influence whether people stay healthy or fall ill. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: A community health nurse notices high rates of typhoid in a rural village. Which intervention best addresses the underlying determinant of health?

options.A: Writing a research paper on the biology of the typhoid bacterium
options.B: Partnering with local leaders to build protected boreholes for clean water
options.C: Telling every resident to boil their drinking water for five minutes
options.D: Opening a large tertiary hospital in the nearest capital city

explanation: Addressing the root environmental determinant, such as unsafe water infrastructure, provides a long-term solution to waterborne disease outbreaks. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the difference between morbidity and mortality?

options.A: Morbidity is caused by bacteria, while mortality is caused by physical injuries
options.B: Morbidity applies only to children, while mortality applies only to the elderly
options.C: Morbidity refers to illness and disease rates, while mortality refers to death rates
options.D: Morbidity measures hospital expenses, while mortality measures community income

explanation: Morbidity tracks how many people are sick with a condition, whereas mortality tracks how many people die from it. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why do children under five suffer the highest morbidity and mortality rates from malaria and diarrhea in many developing regions?

options.A: Children consume more medication than adults, leading to toxic reactions
options.B: Their immune systems are still developing and they face environmental vulnerabilities
options.C: Medical researchers focus exclusively on adult diseases instead
options.D: They are more likely to refuse treatment given by community health workers

explanation: Young children have immature immunity and often live in environments with limited access to clean water and prompt malaria treatment. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of conducting a windshield survey?

options.A: To survey patients sitting in the waiting room of a primary health center
options.B: To repair damaged vehicles belonging to the local health clinic
options.C: To test the blood pressure of every driver passing through a checkpoint
options.D: To directly observe neighborhood environmental and housing conditions firsthand

explanation: A windshield survey allows the nurse to collect real-time visual data about community infrastructure, sanitation, and living conditions. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why is it important to use a combination of methods like interviews and data reviews when assessing a community?

options.A: It prevents community members from speaking directly with nurses
options.B: Government regulations require at least five different reports for every village
options.C: It ensures that every single resident is interviewed individually by a doctor
options.D: It provides a complete and balanced picture of health needs from multiple angles

explanation: Combining statistical data with the lived experiences of community members ensures the true health priorities are identified accurately. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the core philosophy of Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Bringing essential health services as close as possible to where people live
options.B: Focusing treatment exclusively on patients who can pay cash
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid for community survival
options.D: Building high-tech specialist hospitals in major metropolitan cities

explanation: PHC emphasizes grassroots accessibility, making basic health promotion and disease prevention available to everyone in the community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: A community nurse wants to reduce childhood vaccine drop-out rates in a rural district. Which PHC strategy is most appropriate?

options.A: Waiting for parents to bring their sick children to the urban teaching hospital
options.B: Publishing a warning notice about parents who fail to immunize their kids
options.C: Closing down local health posts to consolidate staff in the regional capital
options.D: Training local volunteers to mobilize mothers and setting up mobile immunization posts

explanation: Community participation and outreach are core PHC strategies that overcome geographic and informational barriers to vaccination. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main goal of evaluating population health programs?

options.A: To write promotional brochures for the local government ministry
options.B: To find staff members to blame when a project runs out of money
options.C: To increase the cost of medical services for community residents
options.D: To determine whether the health interventions actually achieved their intended goals

explanation: Evaluation measures the real-world impact of health programs so nurses know what is working and what needs improvement. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)

question: If a community health nurse notices that immunization rates remain low despite running a vaccination campaign, what should be done next?

options.A: Investigate the barriers causing the low uptake and adjust the strategy
options.B: Report the village to the police for failing to cooperate
options.C: Pretend the campaign was a success and submit fabricated data reports
options.D: Assume the community does not care about health and stop all programs

explanation: Evaluation is an ongoing feedback loop; when targets are missed, nurses must analyze the root causes and modify their approach. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T6#GNS124_U1_T6_h7)
